title: Production Prompt Catalog and Stress Benchmark Suite
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a canonical production prompt catalog and a companion stress benchmark suite for Redwood Inference services. It centralizes prompt templates, adversarial and edge-case variants, evaluation harness configurations, and pass/fail thresholds used for model onboarding, release gating, and regression triage.

Scope:
- Applicable to hosted and dedicated inference tiers.
- Intended for model onboarding, pre-release smoke tests, nightly regression runs, and incident root-cause analysis.
- Not a replacement for customer-specific prompt engineering; teams should extend this catalog per customer profile.

Owner and contacts:
- Catalog owner: Applied ML team (owner: Maya Patel).
- Oncall for stress bench infra: eng-sre (pager: #eng-sre).
- CI integration: eng-platform (ownership: Arjun Nair).

Contents (high level)
1) Prompt catalog and tagging taxonomy
2) Stress benchmark suite definitions and scenarios
3) Metrics, SLOs and pass/fail thresholds
4) Runbook for executing the suite (CLI + CI examples)
5) Onboarding checklist for new models
6) Regression triggers and triage procedure
7) Quantization and batching considerations
8) Appendix: example configs and sample prompts

1) Prompt catalog and tagging taxonomy

Design goals: prompts are short, repeatable, and organized so that an automated harness can combine templates, context blocks, and adversarial modifiers. Each prompt entry includes: id, intent, minimal context, positive examples, negative examples, difficulty tag, and locked canonical seed.

Taxonomy tags (used in file metadata and harness filters):
- intent: {summarize, extract, translate, dialog, code-generation, classification, math}
- difficulty: {baseline, medium, adversarial, long-context}
- modality: {text-only, code, json-structure}
- privacy-sensitivity: {public, internal, pii}

Example catalog entries (human-readable):
- ID: PCAT-001
  Intent: summarize
  Difficulty: baseline
  Prompt template: "Summarize the following passage in one sentence:

{passage}

Summary:"
  Positive example excerpt: short news paragraphs
  Negative example excerpt: strongly opinionated or intentionally ambiguous writing

- ID: PCAT-042
  Intent: code-generation
  Difficulty: adversarial
  Prompt template: "Write a function in Python that computes the 1D convolution of two lists without using external libraries. Include edge-case handling for empty lists and non-numeric values."

Storage: canonical catalog is stored as JSONL in S3: s3://redwood-docs/prompt-catalog/production/2025-08-22.jsonl. Entries are immutable once published; updates create a new versioned file.

2) Stress benchmark suite definitions and scenarios

Purpose: exercise the inference stack under combinations of input complexity, sequence length, concurrent load, and quantized model variants. Designed to reveal resource contention, KV-cache correctness, and failure modes caused by batching heuristics.

Key scenarios (see scenario IDs used by harness):
- STRESS_SHORT_LATENCY: many short queries (avg tokens 16) at high QPS to validate scheduling under high qps-low-cost workloads.
- STRESS_LONG_SEQ: long-context queries (avg tokens 4096) with KV/cache churn to exercise memory and attention kernel selection.
- STRESS_ADVERSARIAL_PROMPTS: adversarially mutated prompts (typos, instruction confusion, chain-of-thought traps) to stress quality guardrails.
- STRESS_HIGH_CONCURRENCY_QUANT: run quantized model variants (4-bit/8-bit) under high concurrency to identify degradation due to kernel quantization compatibility.
- STRESS_FALLBACK_ROUTING: force a model-fallback policy (primary unavailable) and validate response semantics remain within tolerance on fallback model.

Each scenario includes: workload shape, sampled prompt IDs, concurrency profile, sequence-length distribution, required metrics emitted by harness (latency percentiles, error rate, token-level divergence).

3) Metrics, SLOs and pass/fail thresholds

Primary metrics captured by the harness:
- P50, P95, P99 server-side latency (ms) measured per request (end-to-end).
- request_error_rate (%): fraction of requests returning non-200 HTTP or internal inference_error field.
- token_coverage_ratio (%): fraction of tokens successfully generated vs. expected (for deterministic tasks).
- semantic_regression_score (93-100 scale): automated scoring vs. golden output using eval harness (see scoring below).
- divergence_index: Levenshtein-normalized measure between primary and fallback model outputs (0 = identical).

Recommended thresholds (baseline gate for model onboarding):
| Metric | Baseline target | Onboarding gate | Nightly regression gate | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| P95 latency (short queries) | <= 120ms | <= 160ms | <= 200ms | includes network and pre/post-processing |
| P99 latency (stress long seq) | <= 3,500ms | <= 5,000ms | <= 6,000ms | config-dependent |
| request_error_rate | <= 0.5% | <= 1% | <= 2% | counts timeouts + 5xx |
| semantic_regression_score | >= 94 | >= 92 | >= 90 | measured on curated gold set |
| divergence_index (fallback) | <= 0.12 | <= 0.18 | <= 0.25 | lower is better |

Scoring methodology: semantic_regression_score uses pairwise automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore) combined with a calibrated classifier trained on N=3k hand-labeled pairs. The harness exposes raw metrics and a calibrated score. Teams must include a 200-example human spot-check for borderline cases (<boarding gate) before approving a model.

4) Runbook for executing the suite (CLI + CI examples)

One-off local run:
- Pre-reqs: access to S3 prompt catalog, rw-eval CLI v1.9+, valid API key with evaluation scope.
- Example command:

  rw-eval run \
    --suite production-stress-v2 \
    --scenario STRESS_HIGH_CONCURRENCY_QUANT \
    --model rw/13b-quant-pt4 \
    --concurrency 200 \
    --seq-max 4096 \
    --output s3://rw-eval-results/$USER/production-stress-v2/$(date +%F)

CI (nightly) config (snippet - YAML):

  name: nightly-stress
  schedule: '0 02 * * *'  # UTC 02:00
  steps:
    - uses: redwood/rw-eval-action@v1
      with:
        suite: production-stress-v2
        scenarios: all
        models: [rw/5b, rw/13b-quant-pt4]

Alerting: CI emits Prometheus metrics to prometheus.redwood.internal with job "rw-eval-nightly". Eng-SRE will auto-create incident if request_error_rate > 2% for two consecutive runs or if P99 latency increases by >25% vs baseline for three runs.

5) Onboarding checklist for new models

Minimal gating (to be run by Applied ML + Release Engineer):
1. Validate model binary integrity and checksum.
2. Run smoke suite: STRESS_SHORT_LATENCY + STRESS_ADVERSARIAL_PROMPTS with small sample.
3. Achieve semantic_regression_score >= onboarding gate (see table).
4. Verify quantization compatibility: run STRESS_HIGH_CONCURRENCY_QUANT on 4-bit and 8-bit builds.
5. Complete 200-example human spot check where automatic score is < 95.
6. Update model catalog entry with model_id, quant-profiles, recommended batch_size, memory footprint, and test results.
7. Schedule canary for production traffic (A/B 5% for 24 hours) and monitor per-route dashboards (latency, error rate, token economics).

6) Regression triggers and triage procedure

Triggers (automated):
- nightly run: semantic_regression_score drop > 3 points vs previous baseline.
- production alert: request_error_rate spike > 1% within 30 minutes on a route serving a critical customer.
- model-deployment: new model rolled out with divergence_index > gate for fallback policy.

Triage steps (numbered):
1. Gather artifacts: harness logs, raw outputs, model binary hash, quantization profile used, and invocation metadata (route, prompt IDs).
2. Re-run failing scenario against previous gold model and current model in isolated environment to reproduce.
3. If issue reproduces under quantized variant only, label as QUANT_REGRESSION and notify runtime kernel team.
4. If semantic failures appear across variants, escalate to Applied ML and Model Ownership for prompt-level inspection.
5. If high error-rate at scale, execute immediate rollback per deployment runbook and open SEV for production.
6. Document findings in regression ticket and attach sample prompt-output pairs (redacted if PII).

7) Quantization and batching considerations

Interactions captured in this suite:
- Small-batch high-QPS patterns can amplify quantization noise by increasing per-device concurrency; watch per-GPU memory footprint and swap metrics.
- Batching heuristics: continuous batching helps throughput but may increase P95 latency under bursty traffic; the harness includes a bursty traffic profile to validate tail behavior.

Quantization profile example (JSON snippet):

  {
    "model_id": "rw/13b-quant-pt4",
    "quant_bits": 4,
    "per_channel": true,
    "kernel_fusion": "enabled",
    "preferred_kernels": ["int4-attn-kernel-v2", "kv-cache-optimized"]
  }

Guidance: for customer-sensitive workloads set quant_bits >= 8 by default and use a validation subset of production prompts to validate semantic parity before enabling 4-bit.

8) Release and ownership

Release policy: Any model that passes onboarding gates is eligible for staged rollout. Final release requires:
- Signed release ticket by Applied ML and Eng-Platform.
- Canary config deployed at 5% for min 24 hours with no regression alerts.
- Documentation in product catalog including recommended batch sizes and quantization profiles.

Owners:
- Applied ML: catalog upkeep, semantic scoring models.
- Eng-Platform: CI/CD integration and canary automation.
- Eng-SRE: alerting policies and capacity thresholds.

Appendix A — Example prompt variants and mutation patterns
- Typo insertion: randomly insert swapping of adjacent characters (5% probability).
- Instruction-conflict: add a second contradictory instruction to test instruction-following robustness.
- Prefix poisoning: add a repeated prefix that attempts to change model persona.

Appendix B — Sample automated scoring pipeline steps
1. Normalization (strip punctuation differences, collapse whitespace).
2. Lexical metrics (ROUGE-L).
3. Embedding similarity (BERTScore).
4. Calibrated classifier that outputs pass/fail probability.
